questions.question: What is React Query (TanStack Query)? Why has it become so popular?
questions.title: React Query Basics — Server-State Library for React
questions.direct_answer:
What is React Query (TanStack Query)? Why has it become so popular?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Server-state caching, stale-time / cache-time, background refetch, dedupe, mutation helpers; separates server state from client state.

**Classic weak answer:** Using Redux to cache server data — overkill; React Query handles caching, dedupe, refetch, and invalidation natively.

**Senior finish:** Explain useQuery/useMutation, queryKey hierarchy, and why server state is fundamentally different from client state.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **React Query Basics — Server-State Library for React** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is React Query (TanStack Query)? Why has it become so popular?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Server-state caching, stale-time / cache-time, background refetch, dedupe, mutation helpers; separates server state from client state**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using Redux to cache server data — overkill; React Query handles caching, dedupe, refetch, and invalidation natively**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Explain useQuery/useMutation, queryKey hierarchy, and why server state is fundamentally different from client state**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Server-state caching, stale-time / cache-time, background refetch, dedupe, mutation helpers; separates server state from client state
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

questions.question: What is the difference between useQuery and useMutation in React Query?
questions.title: useQuery vs useMutation in React Query — Differences Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between useQuery and useMutation in React Query?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** useQuery for reads (cached, background refetched); useMutation for writes (explicit trigger, on-success invalidation).

**Classic weak answer:** Calling useQuery for a write operation — it auto-runs and caches; mutations must be triggered manually and invalidate the right queryKeys.

**Senior finish:** Show optimistic updates with useMutation, onMutate, and queryClient.cancelQueries.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Show optimistic updates with useMutation, onMutate, and queryClient.cancelQueries

questions.question: What are staleTime, cacheTime (gcTime), and query invalidation in React Query?
questions.title: React Query staleTime, cacheTime & Invalidation — Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What are staleTime, cacheTime (gcTime), and query invalidation in React Query?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** staleTime: how long data is fresh; gcTime (v5 rename of cacheTime): how long inactive data stays in cache; invalidateQueries marks stale.

**Classic weak answer:** Setting staleTime to 0 (default) and wondering why refetches happen constantly on window focus.

**Senior finish:** Show patterns for lists + details; explain why gcTime > staleTime; mention queryClient.setQueryData for manual writes.
